insight.insight: Reconstruction-based scoring cannot detect individual false claims, because its objective is indifferent among claim values that yield the same reconstruction. Faithfulness therefore cannot be fixed by improving the reader (verbalizer, reconstructor or probe). It has to be fixed by training the target model so that designated content is decodable against external ground truth. Once that holds, an independent probe can check claims against the model's internals instead of trusting the verbalizer's prose.
dependent_results: Released Qwen-2.5-7B NLA: explanations reconstruct at r̃=0.84, yet only ~2% of salient specific claims are grounded (4.2%/2.1%/1.6% at τ=0.02/0.05/0.10). Paraphrase keeps 0.75 of the score while masking content words drops it to 0.04, so the score rides on gist (§3.1, App. E).

Sandbox: standard training produces co-adapted private codes in 5/5 runs, with grounded-minus-true gaps of 0.30–0.80. Under an independent evaluator, code grounding collapses from 0.53–0.89 to 0.08–0.23. The evaluator gap is 0.17–0.38 for standard runs versus ~0.003 for RECAP runs (§3.2).

Fixes on the reader side fail. Rejection sampling and GRPO raise their proxy while claim-level grounding stays null. A target-side objective that pulls activations toward their own reconstruction collapses decodable content. Frozen probes drift to chance within 1,500 steps, though an affine realignment fitted without labels restores them in 9/9 cases (§3.1, §4).
RECAP in the sandbox: designated content is 100% decodable at +0.001 nats. Fresh NLAs reach ~1.00 truth and grounding under both evaluators, and 0/5 runs show codes (§5.2).

Pythia-160M: fresh probes reach AUC 0.95–1.00 against a 0.77–0.80 control. With K=64 balanced targets the tax is +0.010 nats (CI [-0.015, +0.034]). With K=512 and a naive loss nothing becomes decodable, which balancing fixes (§5.3).

Scale verbalizer: stated-word truth is 0.44–0.46 versus ~0.06 for the control, and recall is 0.29 versus 0.07. The grounded-minus-true gap only narrows, from +0.42 to +0.33. The verbalizer's precision is 0.44–0.63, while a probe at the same recall reaches ~0.80 (§5.4).
Sandbox monitor: verification coverage of designated pre-tap content rises from 37% to 100%. Pythia probe monitor: AUC 0.965 versus 0.823 for the control (§6).

Score-gaming adversary: the r̃-optimal lie suppresses ~87% of the lie penalty, yet the RECAP probe still flags lies at AUC 0.952 while the control falls to 0.508. A probe-aware adversary brings RECAP to 0.909 and the control to 0.242. On never-designated words (ranks 64–128) RECAP has no advantage (0.66 vs 0.70) (§6, App. F).
Decodability erodes within ~250 steps of fine-tuning without the heads. Applying the head loss on every tenth step retains most of it (§5.4, App. C).
key_definitions: NLA: a verbalizer (AV) maps an activation h to text z, and a reconstructor (AR) maps z back to ĥ. Training maximizes cos(AR(AV(h)), h) with the target model frozen (Eq. 1) (§2.1).
Normalized reconstruction: r̃ = (cos(ĥ,h) − floor)/(1 − floor), where the floor is the mean cosine against mismatched activations (§2.1).
Grounding: Δr̃(c) = r̃(z) − r̃(z_¬c) for a minimal-pair flip of claim c. A claim is grounded if Δr̃ ≥ τ. Each edit is validity-filtered (§2.1, App. A).

Grounded-vs-truth cross: crossing grounded/ungrounded with true/false gives four cases. A private code is wording that is grounded but false and specific to the co-trained pair, as revealed by swapping in an independent evaluator. The evaluator gap is r̃_co − r̃_ind (§2.1).

Terms: the tap is the layer and position read. A probe is a freshly fitted linear decoder. Content is designated if it is co-trained via a head and decodable if a fresh probe can read it. Gist is overall meaning as opposed to specific facts. Faithfulness means claim-level truth plus grounding (§2.1).

RECAP: min over θ,φ of L_LM(θ) + w·L_φ(h(θ), y), using linear heads on the tap with external targets y. In the sandbox the targets are slot values. At scale they are a class-balanced presence BCE plus identity CE (Eq. 3) (§5.1).
Tax: held-out LM loss minus that of a shared control, in nats (§2.1).
Sandbox slots: retained, faded (pre-tap), or unread (post-tap, provably absent) (§2.1, App. D).
reasoning_steps: The reconstruction objective has no preference among claim values that give the same reconstruction, so false additions go unpenalized (§1).
The counterfactual flip audit, with validity controls, shows that a released NLA passes via gist with few grounded specifics (§3.1).

Exact sandbox ground truth plus the independent-evaluator swap show a second route to passing: private codes. Because true claims keep their grounding under the swap, the result reflects co-adaptation and not a weak evaluator (§3.2).

Optimizing the reader for grounding only games the proxy. Self-reconstruction on the target side removes information, since freshly retrained probes also fail. Frozen probes go stale while the information persists (§3.1, §4).

Training the target model against external targets avoids all three failures. Co-trained heads leave no frozen probe to drift. External targets leave no self-referential objective to collapse into. Reading the activation directly leaves no text channel for codes (§5.1).

To rule out co-adaptation, every decodability figure comes from independently fitted probes and never from the heads. The naive K=512 shortcut shows why this matters, which yields the design rule that targets must require genuine discrimination (§5.1, §5.3).
Identically trained fresh NLAs on RECAP versus control target models isolate target-model decodability as the cause of the gains in truth and grounding (§5.2, §5.4).
The gap between probe and verbalizer precision at scale motivates trusting the probe over the prose: the verbalizer proposes and the probe verifies (§5.4, §6).

The probe reads the activation, which a text-editing adversary cannot touch. It survives score gaming only when the content is decodable, as the control's collapse shows. The held-out band shows the effect is confined to designated content (§6, App. F).
